findings.title: Catalog create/update/delete endpoints have no authentication and are reachable from the internet via mobile-bff
findings.owner_hint: component: src/Catalog.API/; no CODEOWNERS; top committer Mike Kistler (3/11)
findings.rationale: Root cause: CatalogApi.cs:100-117 maps the four catalog write routes with no authorization metadata, and Catalog.API Extensions.AddApplicationServices never calls AddDefaultAuthentication (unlike Basket/Ordering/Webhooks), so the service has no auth at all. The patch adds AddDefaultAuthentication, puts .RequireAuthorization(policy => policy.RequireRole("Admin")) on PUT v1, PUT v2, POST and DELETE (plain RequireAuthorization is insufficient because any self-registered user can get a token), and passes Identity__Url/Audience/Scopes to catalog-api via the AppHost rather than appsettings (to avoid breaking build-time OpenAPI generation). GET routes stay anonymous. Fails closed if Identity config is missing (auth-tagged endpoints 500). No admin role claim is issued by Identity.API today, so catalog writes are effectively disabled until an operator provisions one. Restricting mobile-bff catalog routes to GET and narrowing SetValues to a DTO are left as follow-ups. Role name aligned to "Admin" (same as bug_03) by the orchestrator after review.
findings.variants_checked: Only four write routes exist in Catalog.API (all covered); GETs intentionally anonymous; Ordering/Webhooks already group-protected (gaps are f001/f002/f011); Basket already authenticated; mobile-bff catalog routes only proxy; overlaps with f031 (CreateItem Id) and f006 (pricing) noted.
findings.bypass_considered: Anonymous write via catalog-api or mobile-bff catch-all now 401; authenticated non-admin now 403; api-version switching does not help since each versioned route carries the policy; missing Identity config makes auth-tagged endpoints fail; forged JWTs fail signature/issuer validation, contingent on f004 being fixed.
findings.test_note: tests/Catalog.FunctionalTests/CatalogApiTests.cs CatalogItemWriteEndpointsRequireAdminRole (401 anonymous, 403 customer, v1 and v2). CatalogApiFixture adds dummy Identity config and a test-only startup filter signing requests in from an X-Test-Role header; CreateHttpClient defaults to role Admin. Conflicts with bug_08 (f031), which edits the same test file and CreateHttpClient callers. Not built or run.
findings.review_reason: CatalogApi.cs adds RequireAuthorization(RequireRole("Admin")) to all four write routes and Extensions.cs adds the AddDefaultAuthentication registration they need, fixing the root cause (no auth in Catalog.API at all). AppHost Identity__* wiring is required; the X-Test-Role middleware is test-only. Owners should know Identity.API issues no Admin role and defines no catalog scope, so writes fail closed for everyone once deployed, and shared ValidateAudience=false leaves the role check as the only guard.

findings.rationale: Root cause OrdersApi.cs:12: the ship route inherits only the policy-less group RequireAuthorization (Program.cs:21-22). Adds an endpoint-level .RequireAuthorization(policy => policy.RequireRole("Admin")), combined with the group policy, so non-admins get 403 before the handler runs. DEPLOYMENT CAVEAT: Identity.API ProfileService issues no role claim and no seeded user has a role, so after this patch nobody can ship via the API until the IdP issues role=Admin to operator accounts (fails closed); the IdP-side change is left as a follow-up. The agent ran `git apply --check` (no writes) despite the read-only brief.

findings.bypass_considered: BFF path hits the same gated endpoint; replayed IdentifiedCommand still passes authorization first; other-audience tokens still need a role=Admin claim the IdP does not issue; the x-test-role header is read only by the test-only AutoAuthorizeMiddleware.
findings.test_note: tests/Ordering.FunctionalTests/OrderingApiTests.cs ShipWithoutAdminRoleIsForbidden (expects 403); AutoAuthorizeMiddleware adds a role claim from an x-test-role header so the two existing ship tests still exercise handler logic. Not built or run.
findings.review_reason: The OrdersApi.cs hunk adds RequireAuthorization(policy => policy.RequireRole("Admin")) to /ship, fixing the vertical privilege escalation at the route; the test-only x-test-role middleware never runs in production and the new 403 test covers the fix. Style docked for the inline policy and hard-coded "Admin" string, and because Identity.API issues no role claim the endpoint refuses everyone until role issuance is added.

findings.rationale: Root cause CreateOrderCommandHandler.cs:44, the only place a persisted Order gets its items, passes client item.ProductName/UnitPrice into Order.AddOrderItem (values originate in CreateOrderRequest.Items via ToOrderItemDTO, which only maps). findings.title: Indirect prompt injection via catalog content plus GetUserInfo tool plus auto-rendered images exfiltrates user PII with zero clicks
findings.owner_hint: component: src/WebApp/; no CODEOWNERS; committers Stephen Toub, Aditya Mandaleeka (1/2 each)
findings.rationale: Root cause MessageProcessor.cs:24: AllowImages turns every model-emitted markdown link/image into a raw with no URL check, rendered as MarkupString at Chatbot.razor:46, enabling zero-click exfiltration. Adds an anchored allowlist (IsProductImageUrl) accepting only the app's own same-origin shape product-images/{int} with optional ?api-version=N.N (ProductImageUrlProvider.cs:8, ChatState.cs:125); anything else is emitted as HTML-encoded literal text. GetUserInfo narrowing, untrusted-tool-output marking and CSP img-src 'self' are left as defense-in-depth; the sink fix alone breaks the chain.
findings.variants_checked: Only MarkupString sink in WebApp/WebAppComponents is Chatbot.razor:46 via AllowImages (fixed). Other sites (CatalogListItem.razor:10, ItemPage.razor:22/79, CartPage.razor:43) use server-built ProductImages.GetProductImageUrl(id) (no fix). ChatState.SearchCatalog/GetUserInfo left unchanged. Injection vector overlaps f003.
findings.bypass_considered: Absolute/protocol-relative URLs fail the ^/?product-images/ anchor; path tricks fail \d+$; extra query params fail the api-version-only anchored query; encoded/whitespace variants fail and render as text. Residual: model can still print PII as visible text, which is not exfiltration.
findings.test_note: tests/Application.UnitTests/MessageProcessorTests.cs plus a ProjectReference to src/WebApp/WebApp.csproj (no WebApp test project exists). Unbuilt; possible Program type collision with other referenced web projects is unverified.
findings.review_reason: Line 24 of MessageProcessor.cs previously emitted for any URL in model output, enabling exfiltration via image requests; the first hunk now emits only when the anchored IsProductImageUrl regex matches, which fits the product-images/{id}?api-version=2.0 URLs from ProductImageUrlProvider.cs:8 and ChatState.cs:125, and HTML-encodes everything else. No new surface; csproj and test hunks are in scope, though the test covers only the reject case and rejected links now render as visible encoded markdown.

findings.title: PUT /api/orders/cancel cancels any user's order
findings.owner_hint: component: src/Ordering.API/; no CODEOWNERS; top committer Aditya Mandaleeka (1/1)
findings.rationale: Root cause CancelOrderCommandHandler.cs:21-27 loads by client OrderNumber and cancels with no ownership check, and CancelOrderCommand carries no caller identity. Because the handler is also used by the internal OrderPaymentFailedIntegrationEventHandler (no HttpContext), identity is placed on the command: CancelOrderCommand gains optional UserId; OrdersApi.CancelOrderAsync always overwrites it with the token sub (403 if missing); the handler resolves the Buyer via IBuyerRepository.FindAsync(UserId) and returns false unless order.BuyerId == buyer.Id (BuyerId because GetAsync does not load the Buyer navigation). A false result reuses the existing 500 'Cancel order failed' response, so no existence oracle. The internal payment-failed path keeps UserId null and still cancels.
findings.variants_checked: Ship (f011) left to sibling; integration-event-only Set*Status handlers need no change; OrderPaymentFailedIntegrationEventHandler works with UserId null; GET (f001) and create (f005) are siblings; IdentifiedCommandHandler only forwards; ClientApp DTO compatible; existing OrdersWebApiTest mocks return "" for userId; functional tests' AutoAuthorizeMiddleware adds sub.
findings.bypass_considered: Body userId (null or another user) is overwritten from the token; missing sub returns 403 before dispatch (prevents impersonating the internal null path); empty sub finds no buyer; accounts with no Buyer row fail; orders with null BuyerId fail closed (owner also cannot cancel in that short window).
findings.review_reason: The handler hunk resolves the caller's Buyer via IBuyerRepository.FindAsync and refuses the cancel when Order.BuyerId differs, fixing the root cause at CancelOrderCommandHandler.cs:25-31; the endpoint sets UserId from the token sub with `command with { UserId = userId }`, discarding any client value. Design weakness: a null UserId skips the check (fail-open by design for OrderPaymentFailedIntegrationEventHandler), so any future HTTP path that builds CancelOrderCommand without UserId would bypass it. OrdersApi hunk header is one line off but applies with offset.

findings.title: IdentityServer RSA signing private key is committed to git and shipped in build output
findings.owner_hint: component: src/Identity.API/; no CODEOWNERS; added by Aditya Mandaleeka (1/1, initial commit fc61f90)
findings.rationale: Root cause: src/Identity.API/tempkey.jwk is a git-tracked RSA private key (added fc61f90), Identity.API.csproj:50 copies it into every build/publish output, and Program.cs:29/:37 disable Duende key management and call AddDeveloperSigningCredential() unconditionally, which loads that file. The diff (1) removes the csproj Content item, (2) gitignores tempkey.jwk so a regenerated dev key cannot be recommitted, (3) restricts AddDeveloperSigningCredential to Development and enables Duende automatic key management elsewhere. NOT in the diff (secret contents deliberately not emitted): git rm src/Identity.API/tempkey.jwk; purge from history (git filter-repo/BFG), force-push, invalidate clones/forks; treat the key as compromised and rotate it in every deployment/image that ran with it, rebuild and redeploy. Ops: Duende automatic key management in production needs a Duende license plus shared key/Data Protection storage for multiple replicas; a Key Vault-backed AddSigningCredential is the alternative. Note: the agent ran `git apply --check` (no writes) despite the read-only brief; eShop working tree confirmed unmodified.
findings.variants_checked: Repo-wide grep for tempkey, AddDeveloperSigningCredential, KeyManagement, AddSigningCredential: only Identity.API Program.cs:29/37 and Identity.API.csproj:50 in code. tempkey.jwk is the only tracked key-material file. Consuming APIs' validation hardening (audience) is separate. f001/f002/f005 depend on token integrity restored here.
findings.bypass_considered: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development still uses a developer credential, but a fresh random per-instance key, not forgeable. Keys from git history or already-published images remain valid until history purge plus rotation. Re-committing a regenerated dev key is blocked by the .gitignore entry.
findings.test_note: tests/Application.UnitTests/IdentityConfigurationTests.cs SigningKeyIsNotCopiedToBuildOutput (Application.UnitTests references Identity.API, so the Content item flowed the key into its output). Needs a clean build for the after-check because PreserveNewest leaves stale copies. The Development/non-Development signing switch is untested.
findings.review_reason: src/Identity.API/tempkey.jwk is tracked and the diff never deletes it; the .gitignore entry has no effect on a tracked file, and in Development AddDeveloperSigningCredential() still loads the committed key from the project directory, contradicting the new 'never committed' comment. The csproj hunk only stops copying to build output, and the new test checks that symptom rather than the key's presence. Non-Development key management change is the right direction (licensing and shared key storage caveats). Orchestrator note: the missing deletion is a consequence of the patch brief forbidding secret contents as removed lines; the author's rationale (not shown to the reviewer) requires git rm, history purge and key rotation. The comment wording 'never committed' should be fixed.

The log line at L126-130 still prints request.UserId (log text only).

findings.bypass_considered: Victim UserId/UserName/Buyer in the body are ignored; missing sub/name claims yield 400 before Mediator.Send; replayed x-requestid only hits the caller's own idempotency path; POST /api/orders is the only route that issues CreateOrderCommand.

findings.title: CreateItem accepts a client-supplied primary key, allowing sequence collisions that block item creation
findings.owner_hint: component: src/Catalog.API/; no CODEOWNERS; top committer Mike Kistler (3/11)
findings.rationale: Root cause CatalogApi.cs:421 (CreateItem) copies Id = product.Id from the body; on a Postgres identity-by-default column the explicit Id does not advance the sequence. The fix removes that assignment so EF lets Postgres assign the Id; Location already reflects item.Id. Companion change: CatalogContextSeed.cs seeds explicit ids, so SeedAsync now ends with a constant setval(pg_get_serial_sequence('"Catalog"','Id'), MAX(Id)+1, false), run outside the if(!Any()) block so existing databases (including attacker-claimed ids) are repaired on startup; idempotent. UpdateItem (v2 PUT /items/{id}) now returns 400 when the body Id differs from the route id instead of a 500 from EF. Anonymous creation itself is f003.
findings.variants_checked: CreateItem fixed; UpdateItem/UpdateItemV1 mismatch rejected (V1 consistent by construction); CatalogContextSeed.SeedAsync sequence repaired; no other body-to-PK copy in src; CatalogBrand/CatalogType use generated ids; overlap with f003 (auth) noted; if f003 adds auth these functional tests will need its auth setup.
findings.bypass_considered: Any client Id is ignored; pre-claimed ids are skipped by the startup setval; mismatched v2 PUT returns 400 before SetValues and PUT never inserts.
findings.test_note: tests/Catalog.FunctionalTests/CatalogApiTests.cs CreateCatalogItemIgnoresClientSuppliedId (v1 and v2); AddCatalogItem and GetCatalogItemPicDoesNotServeFilesOutsidePics updated to read the id from Location. Hunk line numbers computed by hand; not built or run.
findings.review_reason: The CreateItem hunk removes Id = product.Id at line 421 (root-cause fix) and the seed setval hunk is a necessary follow-on because the seeder inserts explicit ids into an IdentityByDefault column; the constant raw SQL adds no input surface. The UpdateItem hunk (-375,7) adds a body/route id check to a different function on the v2 PUT route, which already fails with a 500 when EF refuses the key change, so it is scope creep and should be a separate change. Without it the reviewer would ACCEPT at about 7.
